During this, it becomes a [[Flying]] enemy. |ability2_cooldown = 15 }} ==Description== The '''Heavy Voidling''', internally referred to as '''Elite Voidling''', is a high health enemy that appears in [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] and [[Voidcore Mode|Voidcore]] modes. It has high health and fast speed. It has two abilities: #The first and only ability seen in regular gameplay is ''Stamp of Execution'', where the '''Heavy Voidling''' stomps at a tower in its range of 10, creating a shockwave with a radius of 10 that stuns towers for 2.5 seconds and deals 150 damage to units. #The second ability is ''Lane Switch'', which makes the '''Heavy Voidling''' jump from one path to another, temporarily becoming a [[Flying]] enemy. As there are no maps with more than one path in either mode it appears in, this ability goes entirely unused. ==Logbook Description== "''Heavy Voidlings were created by Void Cultists as a means of remedying their pacifism. In their mind, stealing an unsuspecting Swift and cramming them into a suit of armor may have been questionable at best, but it was for protecting those who embraced the Void. The Cultists felt this was entirely reasonable, however the Swift inside the suit felt differently. The Cultists have noted the Swift’s complaints and will take them into careful consideration at the next ceremony. They have not yet held the next ceremony.''" ==Appearance== The '''Voidling''' has purple skin and neon pink eyes. Both of its arms are cut off. It wears grey armor on its feet, shoulders neck and waist, strapped to it with brown clothing. On its back it has a small black cape. It also has multiple neon pink crystals growing on its body. ==Strategy== *High DPS towers like the [[Juggernaut]], [[Accelerator]], [[Turret]], [[Engineer]] or [[Ranger]] can be used to take it down. **Such towers with [[Stun Immunity]] can be especially useful, as this means they cannot be stunned by the '''Heavy Voidling'''. **Support towers like the [[DJ Booth]], [[Commander]] and [[Medic]] can be used to boost their DPS. *The '''Heavy Voidling''' moves at a fast pace and can be dangerous if not targeted. **Using towers that can stall enemies like the [[Electroshocker]], [[Freezer]], [[DJ Booth]] or [[Hacker]] is recommended to slow it down. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Miscellaneous}} HeavyVoidlingIconIG.png|'''Heavy Voidling''' on its [[Index]] icon. }} ==Trivia== *The '''Heavy Voidling's''' ability to jump between paths goes unused in both [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] and [[Voidcore Mode|Voidcore]] modes as neither mode actually contains maps with more than one path. **This means it can only actually be seen in [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode. **Originally, the '''Heavy Voidling''' did not have this ability while the [[Voidling]] did. Because of this, the enemy got renamed from ''Elite Voidling'' to ''Heavy Voidling'' as Elite is typically used for stronger versions of enemies with base mechanics inherited.[[File:HeavyVoidlingNameProof.png|280px]]
https://x.com/NimTheOne/status/2068735888285106554 *The '''Heavy Voidling''' is unaffected by enemy appearance [[modifiers]], such as [[Talk Like a Pirate Day]]. ==Update History== *'''5 June 2026''' - [[v2.0.0]] ** '''Heavy Voidling''' added, replacing the [[Unknown]]. **{{Bug}} ''Lane Switch'' has broken animations. *'''17 July 2026''' - [[v2.3.0]] **Cash given on death decreased from {{Money|20,000}} to {{Money|16,000}} in [[Voidcore Mode|Voidcore]] mode. ==Notes== {{Hardcore|[[Vindicator]]|Wave 40|[[Elite Soul]], [[Unknown Boss]] & Heavy Voidling|Wave 41|[[Void Knight]] & [[Void Trickster]]|Wave 42}} {{Voidcore|[[Soul Stealer]]|Wave 45|Heavy Voidling|Wave 46|[[Void Knight]]|Wave 47}} {{ZombieNavBox}}
